title: Bayesian Networks of Density Operators
abstract: We study quantum analogues of Bayesian networks on a directed acyclic graph (DAG), distinguishing two constructions for positive definite density operators on finite-dimensional tensor-product Hilbert spaces. The intrinsic construction starts from a joint state and its conditional-independence properties. The extrinsic construction assembles a state sequentially from prescribed local quantum kernels, following an ordering compatible with the arrows of the DAG. For the intrinsic construction, we prove the equivalence of the ordered, local, and global directed Markov properties, together with entropy, recursive-factorization, and logarithmic characterizations. The extrinsic construction always gives a normalized state and recovers each kernel as a conditional on all preceding systems. The same kernel, however, need not be recovered from the marginal on the vertex and its parents; a three-qubit example exhibits this obstruction. We prove that independence of the chosen topological ordering is sufficient exactly for transitive DAGs: every order-invariant kernel family then yields an intrinsically directed Markov state. Finally, we associate a logarithmic candidate with every positive definite state and DAG, prove that it is subnormalized, and show that the trace-one candidate is a directed Markov state. Both the candidate and the excess global information are invariant under DAG Markov equivalence.
summary: This paper develops a theory for quantum Bayesian networks by analyzing how conditional independence structures (defined via density operators) relate to graph structure on a DAG. It distinguishes between two ways of constructing these states—intrinsic and extrinsic—and provides necessary and sufficient conditions using logarithmic identities to characterize true directed Markov states in the quantum domain.
main_problem: The paper studies quantum analogues of Bayesian networks on a Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG), aiming to distinguish between intrinsic and extrinsic constructions for positive definite density operators.
main_result: It proves that the intrinsic construction yields equivalent Markov properties, while the extrinsic one is highly dependent on the chosen topological ordering; furthermore, it characterizes directed quantum Markov states using logarithmic candidates.
method: The authors employ concepts from quantum information theory, including partial traces, Von Neumann entropy, and defining specialized logarithmic conditionals to linearize complex non-linear Markov identities.
model_or_system: The system involves quantum states represented by positive definite density operators ($ho$) acting on finite-dimensional tensor-product Hilbert spaces, structured according to a DAG representing conditional independence relationships.
key_observables: Density operators ($ho$), quantum kernels ($Q_{v|	ext{pa}(v)}$), excess global information ($g_I(D)\sigma$), and the logarithmic candidate $TD(\sigma)$.
important_parameters: The structure of the DAG (transitivity, chordality) dictates the equivalence between different Markov characterizations.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on defining quantum conditional independence ($\perp\!\!\!Q$) via information measures and assuming the existence of positive definite density operators for factorization theorems to hold.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing definitions (e.g., quantum conditional independence using mutual information) to comparing two construction methods (intrinsic vs. extrinsic), culminating in necessary and sufficient conditions for Markov states via logarithmic identities and global information measures.
why_interesting: This work provides a rigorous mathematical framework for applying graphical model concepts, traditionally from classical statistics, to the non-commutative setting of quantum mechanics, which is crucial for understanding quantum causality.
